definitions.explanation: The legal right of a suspect or defendant to refuse to answer questions from the police, prosecutors or the court. In Japan it is guaranteed by the Constitution.

examples.japanese: ⟦{容疑者|ようぎしゃ}→容疑者：15039_yougisha⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{黙秘権|もくひけん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{行使|こうし}→行使：14087_koushi⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The suspect exercised the right to remain silent.

examples.japanese: ⟦{取|と}り{調|しら}べ→取り調べ：31611_torishirabe⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{黙秘権|もくひけん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{告|つ}げられた→告げる：11808_tsugeru⟧。
examples.english: He was informed of his right to remain silent before questioning.

examples.japanese: {黙秘権|もくひけん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦とはいえ→とはいえ：06282_tohaie⟧、⟦{何|なに}も→何も：03874_nanimo⟧⟦{話|はな}さない→話す：00467_hanasu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{不利|ふり}→不利：03603_furi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}う→思う：00492_omou⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: Although there is a right to remain silent, some people think saying nothing will count against them.

notes:
A legal term from ⟦{黙秘|もくひ}→黙秘：08393_mokuhi⟧ (keeping silent) + ⟦{権|けん}→〜権：31354_ken⟧ (right). It appears in news about arrests and trials; the act itself is ⟦{黙秘|もくひ}→黙秘：08393_mokuhi⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {黙秘権|もくひけん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{行使|こうし}→行使：14087_koushi⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to exercise the right to remain silent
- {黙秘権|もくひけん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{告|つ}げる→告げる：11808_tsugeru⟧: to inform someone of the right to remain silent
- {黙秘権|もくひけん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{告知|こくち}→告知：17348_kokuchi⟧: notification of the right to remain silent
